Introduction

A production design system speeds up delivery and keeps accessibility a default. Pair unstyled accessible primitives with semantic tokens and you get a foundation that scales across products without rewriting the hard parts.

Accessible primitives

Primitives should own focus traps, keyboard navigation, and ARIA roles. You style the surface; behavior stays consistent out of the box.

“Accessibility works best when it is the default path, not a checklist at the end.”

Tokens and theming

Keep colors, radius, and spacing in CSS variables. Light and dark modes swap tokens without shipping a theme runtime — consumers stay in control of the look.

Callout

Prefer semantic names (`--primary`, `--border`) over raw hex in components so themes stay portable.

Conclusion

Accessible behavior, flexible styling, and low runtime cost make a stack teams can adopt once and reuse everywhere.
